_readme: Brief queue for scripts/generate-blog-post.js. Each brief is drafted ONCE (status todo -> done) into a draft PR for Sam to edit; merging publishes. A brief has a format (from-sam, printable, seasonal, data), a working title, an angle, and optionally a search query, trusted sources and Sam's notes. Order matters: the first todo brief is drafted next. See blog/EDITORIAL.md.

briefs.title: October half-term planner 2026
briefs.angle: Nine days, two working parents, one sheet of A4. How to plan half-term childcare, one quiet day, and the cost, the Friday before it starts. Built around the free planner at /printables/half-term-planner.pdf.
briefs.notes: Half-term dates vary by council; say so, and don't state specific dates beyond 'late October'.

briefs.title: The family Christmas countdown, working back from the 25th
briefs.angle: A week-by-week timeline from mid-November: last posting dates, the school nativity, who's hosting, food orders. The point is doing each thing once, in the right week.
sources: Royal Mail last posting dates (check the current year)

briefs.title: The school morning that runs on its own
briefs.angle: Most morning chaos is decided the night before. Three evening decisions (clothes, bags, breakfast) and one rule for the car.

briefs.title: How many after-school clubs is too many?
briefs.angle: A practical test for when the week is overbooked: count the evenings with nothing in them. Opinionated, kind, no judgement of busy families.

briefs.title: Splitting childcare across the school holidays
briefs.angle: Two working parents, a grandparent, a holiday club: how to lay out the six weeks early and fairly, and what to agree before anyone books leave.
briefs.notes: Timely around Easter and May for the summer.

briefs.title: The January household reset: one hour, one list
briefs.angle: Not resolutions. One hour in the first week of January putting the year's fixed dates in the calendar: birthdays, renewals, term dates, MOT, the boiler service.

retiredKeywords: how to share a calendar with family
how to remember birthdays and gifts
